RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel may reflect institutional shortcomings or breach university hiring policies, and implicit affinity bias is a documented challenge in economics. However, panel composition alone does not prove discrimination. The department may have legitimately prioritized specific industry experience or interview performance over publications and degree completion.

Rather than alleging bias outright, first follow up politely on your request for written feedback. Simultaneously check institutional policies to see if gender-diverse panels are mandated. If regulations were breached, you can raise procedural non-compliance through an ombudsman or union representative. Accusing the panel of bias without documentation or official feedback risks reputational damage in a tight academic job market.
